subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should macOS package updates short-circuit same-version/manual no-op runs and broaden stale launchd updater cleanup to include `ai.openclaw.manualupdate.*`, or should same-version refresh remain supported with a stronger durable handoff/recovery contract?
rationale: Current tests and docs preserve same-version package refresh behavior, while the live report shows that behavior can be harmful under launchd; changing it is a product/update-lifecycle decision rather than a purely mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Short-Circuit And Clean Up Stale Jobs
options.body: Treat same-version manual/package update runs as no-op before stopping the Gateway, add carefully bounded cleanup for shipped updater label families including `manualupdate`, and require real macOS LaunchAgent proof.

options.title: Keep Refresh, Harden Recovery
options.body: Preserve same-version refresh semantics, but require a durable handoff, dedupe/serialization, health verification, and recovery path that prevents repeated Gateway termination.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Trackers
options.body: Keep this issue open but split stale label cleanup, duplicate update serialization, no-op update policy, and node-host recovery into separate owner-reviewed issues before implementation.

recommendation.title: Short-Circuit And Clean Up Stale Jobs
recommendation.body: Treat same-version manual/package update runs as no-op before stopping the Gateway, add carefully bounded cleanup for shipped updater label families including `manualupdate`, and require real macOS LaunchAgent proof.
